topic_name: Political Parties, Party Systems and Movements

211.question: The defining goal of a political party, as compared with an interest group, is...

options.A: Mandatory representation of a single profession
options.B: Participation in winning and exercising state power
options.C: The direct resolution of judicial disputes
options.E: Defending any private interest without aspiring to power

213.question: A professional association provides expert information to a parliamentary committee in order to have a bill amended. This is an example of...

options.A: An election commission taking the place of a political party
options.B: The direct exercise of state sovereignty
options.D: An association independently adopting a law
options.E: An association turning into a judicial body

214.question: Voluntary associations created specifically to represent interests are classified as ... groups.

215.question: An institutional interest group is distinguished from a spontaneous association chiefly by...

options.A: The mandatory illegality of its methods of influence
options.B: A refusal of regular interaction with the authorities
options.C: A stable organization and a professional apparatus
options.D: An exclusively emotional bond among the participants

216.question: A party's electorate differs from its formal membership in that it includes...

options.A: Only deputies elected on the party list
options.B: Voters who vote for the party regardless of membership
options.C: All residents of the territory irrespective of how they vote
options.D: Only the staff of the paid party apparatus
options.E: Exclusively the members of the highest party body

217.question: The functions of a political party:

options.C: Adopting generally binding laws by the party's own decision
options.E: Passing legally binding judgments in political disputes

221.question: An organization operates around a committee of influential politicians, has free membership and becomes active in the run-up to elections. This is a ... party.

222.question: Features of a mass party in Duverger's typology:

options.D: Predominantly free membership with no statutory recording
options.E: An amorphous structure around a committee of professional politicians

223.question: In the typology described, a strictly centralized party is distinguished by...

options.A: Handing all decisions over to outside independent experts
options.B: A chance coalescence around a single bill
options.C: The absence of mandatory party discipline
options.E: A combination of ideological unity with a rigid hierarchy

225.question: The number of parties alone is not enough to characterize a party system because...

options.A: It does not reveal the real competition and the nature of relations with the state
options.B: The number of parties cannot be established empirically
options.C: Legal conditions do not affect party activity
options.D: A party system exists only when there are two parties
options.E: All multiparty systems are equally democratic

227.question: Factors that influence the formation of a party system:

options.D: Only the number of parties, regardless of the rules of access to seats
options.E: Only the formal names of parties, regardless of social cleavages

229.question: The growth of the independent power of the party apparatus in relation to rank-and-file members expresses the tendency toward...

options.A: The withering away of the organization
options.C: The expansion of direct popular rule

232.question: Officials who have obtained state posts by virtue of belonging to a party make up which element of its structure?

options.A: The party apparatus as an internal governing body
options.C: An external group of political supporters

233.question: Which statements about parties and interest groups are correct?

options.A: Winning parliamentary seats exhausts the intermediary role of a party
options.B: Influencing a particular bill is sufficient for an association to be recognized as a party
options.C: Expert participation by an interest group means that it exercises state competence
options.D: Influencing a decision is not the same as directly exercising power
options.E: Both can mediate between citizens and the authorities

234.question: Several parties are registered, but access to government is in practice closed to the rivals of the ruling group. What should be examined first?

options.A: The real competitiveness of inter-party relations
options.B: Only the size of the state's territory
options.C: Exclusively the age of the party leaders
options.D: Only the number of party emblems
options.E: Only the number of participants at party congresses

235.question: Indicate the correct correspondences between a type of party and an organizational feature.

options.A: Strictly centralized: a rigid ideological hierarchy
options.B: Cadre: regular statutory membership as the basis of the organizational structure
options.C: Mass: statutory membership and a stable organization
options.D: Cadre: a committee of influential politicians
options.E: Mass: a committee of elites that is active mainly during elections
